lots.what_it_is: Seven boxed video games: Sega Master System Phantasy Star (9500), Rocky (7002) and Psychic World (7066); Sega Genesis (NTSC) PGA Tour Golf II; PSP UMD Video (a film, not a game) Inglourious Basterds; PS3 Beyond: Two Souls; Xbox PAL Digimon Rumble Arena 2. Phantasy Star carries most of the value.
lots.key_photo_findings: Original photo read directly: all seven spines legible. Phantasy Star 'A Four-Mega Plus Cartridge' 9500, Rocky 'The Two-Mega Cartridge' 7002, Psychic World 7066 with a handwritten red '4' price sticker, PGA Tour Golf II is a Genesis box with US barcode and ISBN 1-55543-851-2, Inglourious Basterds is UMD Video (movie), PS3 Beyond has Australian R18+ classification, Digimon spine marked PAL. A paper ticket at right reads '554' (crop enlarged), which may belong to the neighbouring lot; Gowans lists this as lot 555 'QTY OF ASST VIDEO GAMES' with no description. Only the closed cases are shown, so no cartridge, disc or manual is visible.
lots.condition: Master System boxes grubby and yellowed with edge wear; modern cases look fair. Contents (cartridges, discs, manuals) not shown and unverified.

lots.dropped_entries: Researcher's six PriceCharting entries were all guide figures (correctly kept as ASKING, four kept). Dropped the PAL Mega Drive PGA Tour Golf II guide (wrong region: the lot copy is NTSC Genesis), replaced by a sale from the Genesis page. Dropped the PS3 Beyond guide as not worth listing (sale shown instead). Researcher's rate of 1.50 was a guess; I used 1.43 (live, open.er-api.com, 7 Oct 2026). All guide prices re-read on the pages and match what the researcher said. The SOLD entries are new: individual eBay sales read from the PriceCharting completed-sales tables. Inglourious Basterds UMD is a film, not a game, and was not priced (negligible). No Australian auction results: WebSearch budget was used up, so no searches ran.
lots.guide_summary: Mostly SOLD evidence (eBay sales shown on PriceCharting, mainly UK/EU sellers, prices in USD before postage), plus ASKING guide figures. The low end, AUD 200, adds up the lowest CIB sale of each title in the last 24 months (US$139.84). The high end, AUD 560, adds up the median CIB sales (US$390.04). Best copies have sold for more (Phantasy Star up to US$297). Phantasy Star alone is about US$76 to US$255 boxed. No UNSOLD evidence. Rate 1 USD = 1.43 AUD.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-title CIB sales in 24 months, in USD: Phantasy Star 76.09 + Psychic World 30.49 + Rocky 6.74 + Digimon 21.66 + PGA II Genesis 4.85 + Beyond 0.01 = 139.84 x 1.43 = AUD 199.97; /1.198 = 166.9, rounded down to $165. Flip: conservative resale (below the medians because the boxes are worn): Phantasy Star 150 + Psychic World 60 + Rocky 35 + Digimon 40 + PGA 7 + Beyond 4 = US$296 x 1.43 = AUD 423; less eBay AU fees about 13.4% (AUD 57) and outbound postage of about AUD 48 (4 parcels at about $12) = AUD 318; /2.396 = 132.7, rounded down to $130. Both caps assume the cartridges and discs really are in the cases. If Phantasy Star is box only, both drop by about two thirds. Pickup from Moonah, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: All titles read clearly in the original photo and many matching sales were read on opened PriceCharting pages, but the eBay listings behind them could not be opened, the sellers are mostly overseas, and the contents and completeness of the cases cannot be seen.
lots.question_for_gowans: For lot 555: are the cartridges actually inside the Phantasy Star, Rocky and Psychic World boxes, and are the manuals there (Phantasy Star should have a manual and possibly a map)? Are the discs inside the Xbox, PS3 and UMD cases? The photo also shows a '554' ticket: please confirm all seven games are in lot 555.

lots.key_photo_findings: Original photo read: the Virgin title is Cool Spot (logo and T-70196-50 on spine). The three Master System boxes are white grid style with light soiling. The lot ticket in the photo reads '611', not 610; Gowans lists lot 610 as '7 ASST SEGA GAMES' with no description, which fits the seven games shown. Contents not visible.
lots.condition: Boxes fair with general wear; Quackshot spine badly damaged. Cartridges and manuals not visible or verified.

lots.what_it_is: Cast iron two-seater garden bench, dark green paint, pierced foliage and bird back with an oval medallion of a seated classical woman, scroll arms, hoof feet, pierced scroll seat. Very likely a modern Victorian-style reproduction.
lots.key_photo_findings: Original photo read: lot ticket '620' on the medallion (crop enlarged), which matches. No foundry mark or registration diamond visible in the single front view. Crisp casting and even modern paint point to a late 20th or 21st century reproduction of a common design. Back, underside and joints not shown.
lots.condition: Paint looks sound with minor wear from the front. Joints, bolts, rust and any cracks or repairs not visible.
